concepts.name: parameter
concepts.durableOutcome: Explain how learned parameters turn an input into an output.
concepts.definition: An adjustable part of a network that training changes.
concepts.reason: A recognizer needs settings that examples can improve.
concepts.mechanism: Training nudges parameters so useful outputs become more likely.
concepts.concreteCase: Improve recognition of a handwritten seven.
concepts.problemBeforeName: The recognizer gets the seven wrong and needs something adjustable.

analogy.name: safe and combination
analogy.relationship: Capacity is different from learned access.
correspondence: the safe is the network's capacity
the combination is the learned parameter setting
analogy.limit: A network does not literally try combinations like a person opening a safe.

concepts.boundary: A parameter is not a human-readable rule.
concepts.misconception: A parameter is not a complete memory or written instruction.
concepts.expectedAbility: Explain why training changes parameters and later use can leave them fixed.

retrievals.freshSituation: A trained mail sorter handles tomorrow's envelope.
retrievals.listenerTask: Identify what stays fixed during inference.
retrievals.answerPlacement: The next paragraph answers with parameters.
